name: International Journal of Modern Life Sciences
tagline: Peer-reviewed, open-access research across the life sciences.
about: The International Journal of Modern Life Sciences (IJMLS) publishes original research, review articles, short communications and methods papers across the life sciences: molecular and cellular biology, microbial and immune sciences, systems and translational biology, and applied and computational life sciences. All published articles are freely available to read and download.
faq:
Who can submit? | Researchers, clinicians and students in any medical or surgical field. All authors must approve the submission.
How do I submit? | Register as an author, then use Submit Manuscript. Your submission appears on your dashboard where you can follow its status.
Which article types are accepted? | Original research, systematic reviews, review articles, case reports, short communications and letters to the editor. See Author Guidelines for limits.
Is the journal open access? | Yes. Articles are free to read and download under the licence shown on each article.
How are articles cited? | Each article page shows ready-made Vancouver and APA citations with its DOI.
ethics:
IJMMS follows the recommendations of the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) and the core practices of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE).

Authorship: all listed authors must meet ICMJE authorship criteria and approve the final manuscript. Changes in authorship after submission need written consent from every author.

Ethics approval and consent: studies on humans need approval from an institutional ethics committee and informed consent; animal studies need institutional animal ethics approval. Clinical trials must be registered (for India, the CTRI) before enrolment. Research on recombinant DNA, pathogens, biosafety-level materials and genetically modified organisms needs institutional biosafety committee approval, and datasets, sequences and materials should be deposited in recognised public repositories where applicable.

Conflicts of interest and funding: authors, reviewers and editors must disclose financial and non-financial conflicts and all sources of funding.

Originality: manuscripts must be original, not under consideration elsewhere, and are screened with similarity-checking software before review. Duplicate publication, fabrication, falsification and plagiarism lead to rejection or retraction.

Corrections and retractions: errors are corrected through a published correction; seriously flawed or unethical work is retracted following COPE guidance.
aipolicy: Authors must disclose any use of generative AI or AI-assisted tools in preparing a manuscript (what tool, and for what purpose). AI tools cannot be listed as authors and authors remain fully responsible for the content, including accuracy of references. Reviewers and editors must not upload confidential manuscripts to public AI tools.
peer: Every submission is screened by the editorial office for scope, ethics statements and similarity. Suitable manuscripts are sent to independent reviewers, who submit a recommendation (accept, minor revision, major revision or reject) with comments to the author. The editor makes the final decision. Reviewers must declare conflicts of interest and treat manuscripts as confidential.
aims:
IJMLS publishes peer-reviewed research that advances understanding of living systems and their application to health, medicine, agriculture and the environment.

Objectives: to provide a rigorous, freely accessible platform for original research, reviews, short communications and methods papers; to encourage reproducible, ethically conducted studies with transparent reporting of methods, data and materials; and to give researchers, clinicians and students dependable evidence for research and teaching.

Scope: molecular and cellular biology, genetics and genomics, microbiology and immunology, physiology and neuroscience, pharmacology and toxicology, nutrition, biotechnology, bioinformatics and computational biology, stem cells and regenerative medicine, and biomedical engineering, with emphasis on work of biomedical relevance.
subjects: Life Sciences: Biochemistry; Molecular Biology; Cell Biology; Genetics & Genomics; Proteomics & Metabolomics; Biophysics; Stem Cells & Regenerative Medicine; Cancer Biology; Microbiology; Virology; Parasitology; Immunology; Vaccinology; Physiology; Anatomy & Developmental Biology; Neuroscience; Basic Pharmacology; Toxicology; Nutrition & Food Science; Biomedical Engineering; Biotechnology; Bioinformatics & Computational Biology; Pharmaceutical Sciences & Drug Discovery; Environmental & Ecological Health; Biostatistics.
plag: All submissions are checked for textual similarity with similarity-detection software before peer review. Manuscripts with unacceptable overlap, duplicate publication or unattributed text are returned to the authors or rejected. Confirmed misconduct after publication is handled by correction or retraction following COPE guidance.
